Emergency shelter

Exposure kills faster than hunger. Build shelter before anything else, within the first hour of an emergency.

Site selection

Avoid ridge lines, dry riverbeds and dead trees. Look for natural wind breaks, dry ground and materials within reach.

Simple designs

A tarp lean-to staked at a forty-five degree angle reflects a campfire's heat. A debris hut piled a metre deep of leaves insulates below freezing.

Insulation

The ground steals heat faster than cold air. Always put a thick layer of boughs or cardboard under you, not just over you.
